problem: The network is 2–3–1, so the output unit has three inputs, but the XOR construction defines only h₁ and h₂ and writes y = step(h₁ − h₂ − 0.5). The third hidden unit and its outgoing weight w₃ are left unspecified, so a student cannot see how the 13-parameter count matches the 2-hidden-unit XOR circuit.
fix: Add one line: the third hidden unit may produce any value, and its weight to the output is set to 0 (so y = step(1·h₁ − 1·h₂ + 0·h₃ − 0.5)); the 13 parameters are counted for the full 2–3–1 network.

problem: The statement is given without the nonlinearity condition, so it reads as if a single hidden layer with linear activation would also qualify, which contradicts the exam trap on linear layers collapsing.
fix: Say: one hidden layer with a nonlinear activation and enough units can approximate any continuous function on a bounded region to any desired accuracy; the result says nothing about how many units are needed or whether training will find the weights.
